narration: Welcome to the Arms & Armour gallery, where we have a fascinating Mughal ceremonial shield, accession number NM 63.5/9. This round hide shield, or dhal, dates from the 17th‑18th century and was crafted in North India from leather and steel, measuring 46 centimetres in diameter. It features four raised steel bosses and a simple floral border painted on the hide, a design that would have added both protection and visual splendor to a noble’s procession. While the exact workshop and construction technique remain to be researched, the shield offers a glimpse into the martial artistry of the Mughal era.
